title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO esummary for all 9 linked series (SuperSeries GSE298940, 36 samples total) and FTP file listings for 3: GSE289369 has 2 Cell Ranger h5 matrices (KO 147 MB, WT 149 MB, i.e. 2 samples); GSE333844 (APOE4 scRNA-seq, 6 samples) is one 654 MB tar; GSE289365 is an 87 KB table of differentially expressed genes. Other series: CUT&Run (3 samples), ChIP-seq (1), bulk RNA-seq of endothelial cells (6) and aorta (6), vascular scRNA-seq (4).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was seen. Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500 and the supplement was not retrievable. The source of the human perivascular macrophage and Alzheimer's data (public atlas or controlled access) was not established.

a1_downloadable.note: The mouse GEO series are public and downloadable (seen in the FTP listings). Access to the human data is unknown.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only label is the experimental condition (cMAF knockout vs wild type, APOE4 vs control), assigned per mouse. There is no measured outcome column, and any per-cell target such as cell type or perivascular macrophage identity would have to be built by clustering.

a3_inputs_present.note: Count matrices are present as h5 files (seen in the listing).

a4_units_stated.note: Raw UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts from Cell Ranger, the standard 10x Genomics pipeline. Assumed from file names, not opened.

a5_enough_rows.note: The independent unit is the animal: 1–6 samples per series (2 in GSE289369, 6 in GSE333844), 36 samples across the SuperSeries. Cell counts were not opened, but cells from one mouse are not independent labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Small enough for a laptop. Sizes are from the FTP listing.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without the full text. Sample counts were seen in GEO only.

a8_label_provenance.note: Genotype is set by the experiment, so it is not circular. But it is not a prediction target worth modelling.

backbone.name: scGPT / Geneformer (single-cell foundation models)
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible for embedding a few thousand cells

honest_claim_h3: With 1–6 mice per condition, a model could at most tell knockout cells from wild-type cells within these few animals. That is a differential-expression result, not a generalisable prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression of brain macrophages to predict whether the cell came from a cMAF-knockout or wild-type mouse.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-cell gene expression counts from 2 mice (one knockout, one wild type) in GSE289369, plus 6 samples in the Alzheimer-related APOE4 series. The cell count was not opened.
plain_idea.predict: The mouse's genotype, which was set by the experimental design.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little. Differential expression already answers this question, and with so few animals any classifier would learn mouse-level batch effects rather than biology.

ml_idea: None viable. This is a mechanistic knockout study with small mouse cohorts. At most, its perivascular macrophage cells could serve as a reference for annotating cell types in larger brain atlases.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because the project fails Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count independent animals per condition: 2 samples in GSE289369, already seen in GEO.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic knockout study: 36 GEO samples across 9 series, 1–6 mice per experiment. The only label is the genotype the experimenters assigned, so it fails A2 (no measured outcome column) and A5 (the independent unit is the animal).
